title: Cygnus Enterprise — encryption & access safeguard review
summary: Initial security posture discovery for Cygnus evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus on SOC 2/ISO proof, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC scoping, audit/log export, and KMS/HSM model for key custody. Customer leaning toward private or dedicated because of data residency and HSM requirements but wants pricing and a pilot path for hosted first.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-25 08:00 PT
Duration: 28 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood CS), Maya (Cygnus Sec), Tom (CTO), Lena (Infra), Ravi (Compliance)

Summary/Intro: quick intros, agenda set to cover certs, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and retention.

[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick round robin — I'm Sofia, AE — Ethan is our SE, and Noah from customer success is on for a quick note. Maya, Tom, Lena, thanks for taking the time.

[02:00] Maya (Head of Security): Thanks. We'll go over high level requirements first — we're assessing whether Redwood hosted will suffice or if we need Dedicated or Private. Main constraints: SOC two evidence, on-prem H-S-M for key material, SSO via our enterprise S-A-M-L provider, and logs exported to Splunk.

[04:00] Ethan (SE): Great, that helps. On the SOC/ISO side we can share our SOC 2 Type II report — it's in our security pack. For KMS we support several patterns: Redwood-hosted KMS, customer-managed KMS via cloud provider, and we have an H-S-M-backed key custody option in Private deployments — that map's to the dedicated/private conversation.

[06:00] Tom (CTO): Can you explain the difference operationally? I.e. if we go Dedicated what stays in your control vs if we go Private? Our legal team is picky about key custody and seed material.

[08:00] Ethan (SE): Sure. For Hosted, keys by default are managed by Redwood's cloud KMS and we have envelope encryption. In that pattern you don't hold the root keys. For Dedicated — you get reserved capacity, data isolation at compute level, but keys can still be customer-managed in their cloud K-M-S if you set up a VPC peering and KMS integration. Private (VPC or on-prem) — you can bring your own H-S-M, or we can deploy behind your KMS where the root key never leaves your H-S-M; Redwood's control plane can be customer-hosted depending on the package. There's also a middle ground: software KMS with customer-managed keys but that's not H-S-M guaranteed.

[10:00] Lena (Infra): Quick follow — for audit logs, how granular are the logs? We need per-token or at least per-request headers plus model version and route.

[12:00] Noah (CS): Jumping in, our console exposes per-request traces, model version, latency, token counts; audit logs can stream to S3 or to syslog/Splunk via our log forwarder. The exported log includes request id, model id, route, timestamp, and auth principal — PII is redacted by default but we can pass the raw payload if customer chooses.

[14:00] Maya: On the PII point — we need guarantees on not retaining raw prompt text beyond X days and an easy way to purge with proof. How's retention and purge implemented?

[16:00] Ethan: Retention's configurable per-account. Hosted has default 90 days for raw request retention for troubleshooting; Dedicated and Private you can set shorter windows, and Private you control retention fully. Purge is asynchronous — we offer an API to request deletion and we can provide logs showing deletion ops. Note sometimes third-party backups (snapshots) may have longer windows — we can include that in the deletion S-L-A.

[18:00] Ravi (Compliance): We also have legal holds sometimes. Need the ability to suspend deletion for scoped accounts. Is there a way to freeze retention for litigation hold?

[20:00] Ethan: Yes, we support legal-hold flags at the tenant level in Dedicated/Private. Hosted can support with SLA addendum; it's something we coordinate with legal.

[22:00] Tom: What about RBAC? Our org needs role scoping: devs should not be able to see production prompts, and redwood role mapping to our IdP groups is critical.

[24:00] Sofia: We support S-C-I-M provisioning for groups and SAML mapping to roles. RBAC can be set per-project/route — you can lock models to a team. We also have token scoping so service tokens only have model-invoke permissions, not admin permissions.

[26:00] Maya: A few micro details — do audit logs contain full prompt payloads by default? We need them masked.

[27:00] Ethan: Default behavior masks PII, but you can opt-in to full payload logs for troubleshooting. For compliance we recommend using redaction hooks or local pre-processing to strip sensitive fields before sending. In Private deployments there's the cleanest guarantees.

[27:30] Sofia: Okay, wrap up: we'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs, Ethan will put together an architecture diagram showing H-S-M flow with Dedicated and Private, and we'll schedule a security deep dive next week with our security engineer. Any other ask?

[27:50] Maya: Please include exact log field schema and sample Splunk forwarding config. Also, cost delta between hosted pilot and dedicated with customer-managed KMS.

[28:00] Sofia: Noted — we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms may be off (H-S-M transcribed as 'H S M', SAML as 'S A M L', SOC2 as 'SOC two') and occasional filler.
